item.title: New regulations to benefit cross-Strait travelers, spokeswoman says
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
New regulations to benefit cross-Strait travelers, spokeswoman says A spokeswoman for the Chinese mainland stated that new regulations on exit and entry administration, which took effect on Tuesday, are intended to protect the lawful rights and interests of travelers and provide a better legal environment for cross-Strait exchanges, countering concerns raised by Taiwan authorities. Taiwan's "Mainland Affairs Council" has warned that some provisions could pose risks for certain groups traveling to the mainland. Zhu Fenglian, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a news conference on Wednesday that the regulations aim to standardize exit and entry administration, safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of travelers, and protect national sovereignty, security, and development interests. She stated that the regulations mainly improve mechanisms for preventing security risks related to outbound travel, require that reasons given in entry and exit applications be truthful and lawful, and regulate intermediary services. The measures are designed to protect the lawful rights and interests of people on both sides of the Taiwan Strait and provide Taiwan residents with a better legal environment for traveling to the mainland, Zhu said. She added that Taiwan residents traveling to the mainland for tourism, family visits, exchanges, and other lawful purposes could do so normally as long as they comply with relevant laws and regulations. Zhu criticized the Democratic Progressive Party authorities for what she described as exaggerating risks and misleading the public to restrict cross-Strait exchanges. She claimed such warnings were intended to discourage interaction between people on both sides and prevent Taiwan residents from gaining a fuller understanding of the mainland. Zhu also cited continued cross-Strait travel as evidence of strong demand for exchanges. According to statistics from the Taiwan Affairs Office, Taiwan residents made 2.85 million visits to the mainland in the first half of this year, up 24.9 percent year-on-year. She said the growing number of visits showed that cross-Strait exchanges remained active despite restrictions and warnings from the DPP authorities.

item.title: Mainland criticizes Taiwan's educational 'de-Sinicization'
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
Mainland criticizes Taiwan's educational 'de-Sinicization' A Chinese mainland spokeswoman on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities for their long-standing efforts to promote "de-Sinicization" in education and remove elements of traditional Chinese culture from school curricula. Zhu Fenglian, spokeswoman for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated that the DPP authorities' push for "de-Sinicization" in education and "cultural Taiwan independence" has had serious consequences. Chinese culture is the spiritual home of Taiwan compatriots and a source of strength for Taiwan's economic and social development, Zhu said. She noted that several classical Chinese texts had been removed from school curricula in Taiwan, leaving students with fewer opportunities to study such works. Some students also lacked knowledge of historical figures, including Zhuge Liang, a well-known strategist during the Three Kingdoms period (220-280), as well as major historical events such as the Nanjing Massacre committed by Japanese invaders in East China's Jiangsu province. "This is not the children's ignorance, but the wrongdoing of 'Taiwan independence' forces," Zhu said. She warned that continued efforts to distance education in Taiwan from Chinese culture would weaken the cultural roots of people on the island and deprive Taiwan society of the nourishment of traditional Chinese culture. Zhu mentioned that people from various sectors in Taiwan had expressed concern over the issue, and that a growing number of Taiwan residents opposed "cultural Taiwan independence" and "de-Sinicization" in education. She added that they hope the situation can be corrected, with a sound curriculum put in place to carry forward fine traditional Chinese culture and safeguard the cultural and spiritual heritage of Taiwan compatriots.

item.title: Taiwan's future must be decided by all Chinese people: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
Taiwan's future must be decided by all Chinese people: spokesperson BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- Taiwan's future can only be determined by the over 1.4 billion Chinese people, including Taiwan people, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a press conference in response to a media query about recent comments by a Taiwan official, who claimed that Taiwan's future must be decided by its 23 million people. The Taiwan question is a scar left over by a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) party about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Strait in prolonged political confrontation. However, the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. Noting that there is only one China in the world, Zhu stressed the irresistible trend of national reunification. "The future of Taiwan rests solely with the more than 1.4 billion Chinese people, including Taiwan compatriots," she added. Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party authorities have clung to their separatist stance of seeking "Taiwan independence," refused to recognize the 1992 Consensus that embodies the one-China principle, and worked to disrupt cross-Strait exchanges. These actions run counter to the mainstream will and are opposed by people from both sides of the Taiwan Strait, Zhu said. The mainland, in contrast, has continuously promoted cross-Strait exchanges, cooperation and integrated development. "Our policies toward Taiwan remain clear and consistent. We will safeguard the interests and well-being of Taiwan compatriots, and work resolutely to advance national reunification," the spokesperson noted.

item.title: Mainland slams Taiwan's DPP for marginalizing traditional Chinese culture in education
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
Mainland slams Taiwan's DPP for marginalizing traditional Chinese culture in education BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) for trying to reshape education along its secessionist line, warning that such actions could leave Taiwan detached from its Chinese cultural heritage. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks at a regular press conference in response to a question about the DPP authorities' long-running efforts to reduce Chinese cultural elements in education and remove classical Chinese texts from school curricula and textbooks. Zhu said the DPP authorities' secessionist education has had "serious consequences." Chinese culture constitutes an essential part of the spiritual heritage of Taiwan people and has provided cultural impetus for the island's economic and social development, she said. When Chinese cultural traditions are severed on the island and classical Chinese works are removed from textbooks, Taiwan students will have fewer opportunities to study Chinese classics and learn about important historical figures and events in school, Zhu said. "This is not children's fault that they are ignorant about Chinese history and tradition but the fault of the 'Taiwan independence' forces," Zhu said. With "education reform" starting in the 1990s amid a rising secessionist narrative, the changes to curriculum and textbook guidelines in Taiwan have been highly political, aimed at removing Chinese cultural elements and severing historical ties with the Chinese mainland. Taiwan adopts a textbook selection system in which the education department issues guidelines on what should be included in textbooks, and schools can then choose from different editions of textbooks that follow the guidelines. With the implementation of the 2019 guidelines, the number of recommended classical texts for senior high school students has been reduced to 15 from 30 recommended by the previous guidelines. Several landmark works that are important for Chinese identity and values are no longer on the recommended list. Before the 2019 textbook guidelines, Taiwan's history textbooks generally followed a chronological structure, starting from the birth of Chinese civilization and covering various imperial dynasties before reaching contemporary history. Under the current senior high school curriculum, Chinese history is more often taught as part of a broader East Asian and regional history, with greater emphasis placed on Taiwan's history. Many educators and parents on the island have repeatedly voiced their concerns about the rising secessionist tendency in education. Some of them have operated an association and a website since 2018 to compile and teach history and Chinese language courses themselves.

item.title: Mainland says Taiwan's DPP shifts blame for halt of cross-Strait dialogue
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
Mainland says Taiwan's DPP shifts blame for halt of cross-Strait dialogue BEIJING, Sept. 16 (Xinhua) -- Cross-Strait institutional dialogue was suspended because Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities rejected its political foundation, which is the one-China principle, a mainland spokesperson said on Wednesday. Previous cross-Strait consultations had been conducted on the basis of the 1992 Consensus, which embodies the one-China principle, said Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, in response to the DPP's claims that the mainland had unilaterally halted institutionalized consultations and restricted travel and exchanges. The DPP, since coming to power in 2016, has adopted a secessionist line and refused to recognize the 1992 Consensus, which "unilaterally undermined" the basis for cross-Strait dialogue, leading to the suspension of institutionalized talks and communication mechanisms, she noted. Furthermore, the DPP authorities have restricted cross-Strait travel and cooperation in various fields, she said, adding that such measures had impacted the interests of people and businesses in Taiwan. "The DPP is accustomed to distorting facts, shifting the blame and turning accusations back on others," she said. The Taiwan question stems from a full-blown civil war fought between the forces led by the Communist Party of China (CPC) and the Chinese Kuomintang (KMT) about eight decades ago. In 1949, the remnants of the defeated KMT retreated to Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China was founded under the leadership of the CPC. The unresolved civil war and foreign interference have left the two sides of the Taiwan Strait in a prolonged state of political confrontation, though the fact that Taiwan is an inalienable part of China's territory has never changed. The two sides had established institutionalized communication channels and reached agreements on a range of issues before the DPP took office in 2016. The mainland has repeatedly called for resumption of cross-Strait dialogue on the basis of the 1992 Consensus. Regarding the mainland's new regulations governing entry and exit, which took effect on Sept. 15, Zhu said these regulations would provide a clearer legal framework for travel between the mainland and Taiwan. Repeated warnings from the DPP authorities about the new regulations were only aimed at deterring Taiwan residents from visiting the mainland, to prevent them from seeing through the DPP's disinformation attempts, she said. About 2.85 million visits to the mainland by Taiwan residents were recorded in the first half of 2026, up 24.9 percent year on year. "The steady flow of Taiwan people traveling between the two sides is the clearest demonstration of how absurd the DPP authorities' efforts to restrict and obstruct cross-Strait exchanges are," she said.

item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi Conducts Visits, Services and Policy Briefings in Yulin: Practical Policies and Heartwarming Services Boost Confidence among Taiwan Compatriots
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi Conducts Visits, Services and Policy Briefings in Yulin: Practical Policies and Heartwarming Services Boost Confidence among Taiwan Compatriots Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-18
Sep 18(Taiwan.cn)—Recently, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Guangxi held a policy briefing in Yulin City to explain the Party's policies, laws and regulations concerning Taiwan, as well as preferential policies and measures benefiting Taiwan compatriots. Around 100 participants attended the event, including representatives of Taiwan-invested enterprises and Taiwan businesspeople residing in Yulin, mainland spouses of Taiwanese nationals, relatives of Taiwan compatriots, Taiwan teachers working in Yulin, and officials from relevant municipal departments. The briefing addressed issues of greatest concern to Taiwan compatriots. Legal experts systematically reviewed laws and regulations related to Taiwan affairs and provided in-depth explanations supported by practical cases involving Guangxi's preferential policies for Taiwan compatriots. Officials from the Yulin Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau elaborated on policies covering employment, entrepreneurship, talent introduction and social security support for Taiwan compatriots. Staff from the Yulin Municipal Tax Service explained preferential tax policies for Taiwan-invested enterprises item by item. The informative and pragmatic briefing was praised by participating Taiwan compatriots as "highly informative." Following the briefing, Taiwan compatriot attendees visited the Guangxi headquarters of Want Want Group, the R&D headquarters of Fuchang Group and the Yulin Association of Taiwan-invested Enterprises. They gained first-hand insights into the operations and development of key Taiwan-invested enterprises by visiting their production sites. During exchanges, participants stated that they would remain confident in development, seize opportunities and continue to expand their investments in Yulin. (Jointly reported by Taiwan.cn and the Taiwan Affairs Office of Yulin Guangxi) Related Stories

item.title: The Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling Visits Taiwan Compatriots Affected by Flood Disaster
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-18
The Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling Visits Taiwan Compatriots Affected by Flood Disaster Source: Taiwan.cnUpdated: 2026-09-18
Sep 18(Taiwan.cn)—On September 16, Li Jian, Member of the Standing Committee of the CPC Tieling Municipal Committee and Director of the United Front Work Department, led a team to visit Mr. Zhu and his wife, Taiwan compatriots residing in Tieling. The team held discussions with them to learn about their production and living conditions, conveying the care and warmth of the Party committee and government. On July 13 this year, Tieling was hit by short-duration heavy rainfall, triggering floods in some areas. Mr. Zhu and his wife, who had returned for a family visit at that time, were trapped. Local authorities activated emergency responses immediately and carried out prompt rescue operations to fully safeguard the lives and property of the Taiwan compatriots. After the flood crisis, the Taiwan Affairs Office of Tieling continued to follow up on their situation, monitoring their health and daily life, and providing consistent follow-up services, allowing the Taiwan compatriots to truly feel the care of the local community. During this trip back to Tieling, Mr. Zhu and his wife came specifically to express gratitude for the timely rescue provided by the local government and fire rescue teams during the flood. During the meeting, Li Jian inquired in detail about their post-disaster physical recovery and their itinerary for this visit to Tieling. He stated that compatriots across the Taiwan Strait share the same bloodline and are closely bonded as family. Offering assistance in times of crisis is the inescapable duty of local functional departments. Whenever Taiwan compatriots return to Tieling, the CPC Tieling Municipal Committee and Tieling Municipal Government will provide thoughtful and dedicated services, act as trusted friends for Taiwan compatriots, and earnestly implement various preferential policies benefiting Taiwan compatriots, so that they can live in Tieling with peace of mind. Mr. Zhu and his wife said with emotion that the timely rescue amid the crisis made them deeply experience family-like warmth and witness the spirit of "compatriots on both sides of the Strait are one family." They found it hard to let go of the kindness and sincere concern in Tieling. They expressed their willingness to share their personal experiences in Tieling with relatives and friends in Taiwan, introduce the real economic and social development of Liaoning Province, encourage more Taiwan compatriots to visit Tieling, and help deepen cross-strait people-to-people exchanges. item.title: Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Chinese mainland spokesperson slams Lai Ching-te's flattering remarks on Japan Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-02-11
BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday denounced Taiwan authorities led by Lai Ching-te for ignoring the heinous crimes committed by Japan during its colonial rule over Taiwan, describing their flattering remarks toward Japan as utterly disgraceful. Zhu Fenglian, spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, made the remarks in response to a media inquiry about Lai's intention to work with Japan to "deal with regional challenges." Zhu also urged the Japanese side to retract Sanae Takaichi's erroneous remarks on Taiwan, handle Taiwan-related issues prudently, and abide by the one-China principle with concrete actions. item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges
item.description:
Published: 2026-02-11
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for obstructing cross-Strait exchanges BEIJING, Feb. 11 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson has condemned Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for imposing restrictions and obstacles on cross-Strait exchanges in pursuit of their "Taiwan independence" agenda and selfish gains. The DPP authorities, led by Lai Ching-te, are the biggest obstacle to cross-Strait interactions and their acts have drawn strong criticism from various sectors in Taiwan, Zhu Fenglian, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, said at a regular press briefing on Wednesday. Zhu expressed the hope that Taiwan compatriots will firmly oppose the retrogressive actions of the DPP authorities and promote exchanges and cooperation across the Taiwan Strait in various fields. She noted that cross-Strait flight routes have been disrupted due to interference from the DPP authorities, with previously operated destinations yet to resume normal operations. In 2025, the average passenger load factor on cross-Strait routes reached 80 percent, reflecting the strong need for direct flights between the two sides of the Strait, Zhu said. "We hope that the Taiwan side will heed public opinion and lift unreasonable restrictions on cross-Strait air transport as soon as possible," she added.

item.title: Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps
item.description:
Published: 2026-01-29
Taiwan's DPP authorities slammed for hyping up security risks of mainland apps Source: XinhuaUpdated: 2026-01-29
BEIJING, Jan. 28 (Xinhua) -- A Chinese mainland spokesperson on Wednesday criticized Taiwan's Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities for hyping up the so-called information security risks of applications from the mainland. Zhang Han, a spokesperson for the State Council Taiwan Affairs Office, stated at a press conference that the DPP moves have deprived people in Taiwan, especially the youth, of their right to know and the freedom to use social networking platforms. Noting that such moves reveal the fear and insecurity of the DPP authorities, Zhang said they will have to face the dire consequences of their wayward actions.
